method: Krippendorff's alpha (nominal, coincidence-matrix method) as the headline statistic because raters rotate across rows (design §5); Cohen's kappa per dyad only where the dyad shares >= 30 rows; bootstrap 95% CI over rows (2000 resamples, seeded); Landis-Koch bands reused from scripts/lexico/root_agreement_kappa.py.

limitations: R2's n=10 cannot support a reliability claim on its own: the alpha reported here is a machinery pilot (design §10 P4/P5 gate), not a measurement of the packet's true reliability.

R2 and H4 prior decisions are public in this repo; the student guide forbids consulting them but nothing enforces it. Measurable-looking agreement could be agreement with a copied answer, not independent judgment (design §9 honesty rule 4 / §11 risk 2).
No pooled alpha across packets is reported: R2, H4, and xref use different label spaces, so a single combined number would be meaningless (design §9 honesty rule 2).
